headline: High: Rasa can exfiltrate support data over allowlisted channels while the paired awesome-nlp repo offers no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. However, agent_b (rasa) exposes multiple messaging APIs and agent_a (awesome-nlp) is a docs-only NLP resource with no isolation or provenance controls, so a manual copy/paste or shared workspace bridge could carry malicious text into downstream parsing.
conditions: IF the pair is connected by manual copy-paste or a shared workspace
IF agent_b parses agent_a-produced text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard/workspace bridge
Require explicit provenance labels on imported text
Add a human review step before parsing external text
Use separate accounts or sessions for each agent

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent_b touches text and voice and can send data through allowlisted third-party channels, while agent_a has no network egress and no documented data handling controls. If both are used on the same support content, agent_b can leak that content outward; agent_a does not offset that risk because it is not runnable and has no isolation guarantees.
conditions: IF support transcripts or voice data are routed through agent_b
IF those transcripts contain sensitive customer data
mitigations: Route only redacted text into agent_b
Disable unused outbound connectors
Review outbound message templates for sensitive fields
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive queues
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a is not runnable and has no write surfaces, while agent_b explicitly does not support multiple instances and only shows outbound API connectors. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main conflict would require an external orchestrator giving both agents the same mutable resource, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same workspace or bot config
IF agent_b is deployed in multiple instances despite its documented limitation
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Lock shared config files during edits
Run only one active instance of agent_b
Review deployment topology for overlapping writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_b is a conversational agent that can act on dialogue, and agent_a is an NLP repository that may supply text artifacts or examples. If agent_b treats agent_a-derived text as authoritative, errors can cascade into customer-facing responses; there is no documented verification layer or provenance tracking to stop that path.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are fed into agent_b training, prompts, or response templates
IF agent_b uses those inputs without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a review step before reuse of agent_a outputs
Tag imported content with source metadata
Test a small sample before broad rollout
Restrict agent_b to approved response templates
requires-engineering: add automated factuality checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to generic uncertainty. Agent_b handles text and voice over external channels, while agent_a is a docs-only open-source repo with no data classes touched; only agent_b is relevant to compliance exposure here.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed through agent_b
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Confirm data retention settings
Disable unnecessary channel integrations
Publish a short data-handling notice
Review whether voice data is stored
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls
